net.open.note: HTTP OPEN sends nothing to the server; helpers.jsonl shows the GET only after the next STATUS

net.status.note: 37 00 00 01: 55 bytes, connected 0 (the local server's whole answer is already in), error 1. The first STATUS performs the GET (HTTP.cpp:430-436)

net.read.note: hello.txt, CR LF line ends untouched (translation 0)

net.read.eof.note: Z80: READ 64 past the end NAKs. C: network_read's own STATUS sees 136 with nothing waiting and returns 0 without sending a READ (network_read_nb.c), so the C log has STATUS only

net.read.loop.note: OPEN, then STATUS 3000 / READ 2048 / STATUS 952 / READ 952 / STATUS 00 00 00 88, CLOSE; prints 3000. C (network_read_nb) sends the same pairs

net.read.ahead.note: READ 2048 with no STATUS first: the GET goes out and 2048 come back; a second READ 2048 ACKs with the 952 that are left. C uses network_bus_read, which returns 2048 both times: fujinet-lib cannot see a short reply (fwspec network_bus_read mismatch)
net.read.ahead.surprise: fwspec READ trap 'HTTP body with nothing buffered: client read short -> NAK and the partial bytes are lost (HTTP.cpp:508-514)' did not happen: FS.cpp:294-297 caps the request to available() first, so a READ larger than what is left returns what is left (ACK, 952 bytes). Only a READ while available() is 0 asks for the full length. Answers open question 1 for fujinet-pc (mgHttpClient)

net.set_parser.note: Z80 sends fields 00 01; fujinet-lib sends 01 01 (field 1 is ignored)

net.parse.note: C: network_json_parse sends SET_PARSER (01 01) again, then PARSE

net.status.parsed.note: 00 00 00 88 right after PARSE, as fwspec says (FS.cpp:398)

net.query.note: QUERY '/name' ACK, STATUS 08 00 00 01, READ 8 = 'FujiNet' 0A. C: network_json_query sends 256 payload bytes (the query plus whatever follows it in memory), then STATUS/READ until 0 waiting, and strips the 0A

net.query.missing.note: QUERY of a name not in the document ACKs; STATUS 00 00 00 88 (nothing queued)

net.write.http_put.note: Z80 writes the body in BODY mode (allowed for PUT, HTTP.cpp:677-683). C: network_http_put = network_http_post, so it sends SET_HTTP_MODE 4, WRITE, SET_HTTP_MODE 0

net.close.http_put.note: the PUT goes out at CLOSE: helpers.jsonl shows PUT /put.txt with body 'PUT from an H89' (15 bytes)

net.open.http_delete.note: Z80 mode 5; C network_http_delete opens with mode 9 (DELETE, headers allowed)

net.status.http_delete.note: 09 00 00 01 ('DELETED' CR LF waiting); helpers.jsonl shows DELETE /old.txt

net.close.unsent.trap: DELETE (and POST) are sent only by a STATUS or READ; CLOSE alone sends nothing (fwspec NET_CLOSE trap, HTTP.cpp:553-564). helpers.jsonl has no request for /never.txt

net.open.http_put_h.trap: aux1 14 'PUT with headers' is normalised to POST (fwspec open_modes 0x0E, HTTP.cpp:125-128): helpers.jsonl shows POST /puth.txt, and the answer GOT 12 BYTES (0E 00 00 01)

net.write.header.note: helpers.jsonl: the GET carries X-Machine: H89

net.read.header.note: STATUS 0B 00 00 01, READ 11 'text/plain' 9B; STATUS 09 00 00 01, READ 9 'H89 book' 9B: alphabetical by lower-cased name (content-type before x-test-server), not the order written, as fwspec says. A third STATUS would read 00 00 00 88; a third READ is not sent (fwspec: reads past the vector)

net.write.note: helpers.jsonl: the board received 'hello from the h89' 0D

net.read.tcp_reply.note: the board echoes a key at a time, so the answer arrives in pieces (e.g. READ 17 'hello from the h8', READ 25 '9 CR LF HELLO FROM THE H89 CR LF > '); the loop reads until 0.5 s pass with nothing waiting, so the last exchange is a STATUS 00 00 01 01

net.status.hangup.note: after BYE, STATUS every 0.1 s until connected = 0: then 0F 00 00 88 - error 136 and the 15-byte goodbye ('BYE', then CR LF 'Goodbye.' CR LF) still waiting to be read (TCP.cpp:215-219)

net.status.listen.note: 00 00 01 01 once the helper has connected: on a listener 'connected' = a caller is waiting (TCP.cpp:225-229)

net.read.server.note: PING CR LF, 1.5 s after the helper connects

net.close_client.trap: inverted: NAK means the client WAS disconnected (close_client_connection returns UNSPECIFIED on success, TCP.cpp:357-370); fujinet-lib returns FN_ERR_IO_ERROR. Waits for the helper's next connection (about 5 s) so a client is still connected when CLOSE_CLIENT goes

net.close_client.none.trap: inverted: ACK when there was no client to close (err 207, TCP.cpp:350-355)

net.get_remote.early.note: before any datagram has arrived: '255.255.255.255:0' 9B 00 then junk, always 256 bytes (answers fwspec open question 3 for fujinet-pc). fnUDP's parsePacket also runs in the background poll after every command, so once a datagram has arrived GET_REMOTE names its sender even before any STATUS or READ - a slower program (the C runs) sees '127.0.0.1:7805' here

net.read.udp.note: Z80: every 0.1 s, STATUS then READ 512; a READ NAKs while no datagram is in (it happened in the first probe run, not in the four captures), and once one is in the READ returns exactly that datagram, 'PING' (4 bytes). C: waits until STATUS shows avail > 0, which needs a SECOND datagram, then network_read(avail) returns the first
net.read.udp.trap: STATUS under-reports (fwspec STATUS trap; open question 2 confirmed): it takes the waiting datagram into the buffer and counts only the next one - in both Z80 captures the STATUS just before READ ACK 4 'PING' says 00 00 01 01

net.set_destination.note: payload 'N:127.0.0.1:7805' 00. C uses fuji_bus_call: network_udp_set_destination sends no NUL and wants 'N7:' (fwspec traps); a probe with 'N7:127.0.0.1:7805' and no NUL ACKed but the datagram never reached 7805

net.read.dir.note: three 43-byte lines, CR LF ended: BLANK H8D, DISK IMG, README TXT
net.read.dir.surprise: every entry shows size 0 (and the fixed 1-01-24 12:00p date); fwspec directory_formats says the short form carries the size. fujinet-pc's SD listing has no sizes (the long form 80H also shows 0)

net.lock.trap: SD cannot lock (SD.cpp:307-317); the reason is lost: STATUS afterwards says 207, not 146 (fwspec fs traps)

net.getcwd.note: 'SD:/test/' - the N8: is gone, no NUL

net.open.relative.note: OPEN 'N8:readme.txt' resolves against the prefix to SD:/test/readme.txt; READ 59 bytes

net.username.note: Z80 sends no fields; fujinet-lib sends two dummy fields 00 00 (ignored)

net.open.translated.note: the same GET with aux2 0, but the override 3 is ORed in and the native EOL is CR: STATUS 35 00 00 01, READ 53 bytes with each CR LF turned to CR

net.set_int_rate.note: Z80 one field (64); fujinet-lib two (64 64). Meaningless on the H89: the data-ready signal goes nowhere

net.set_int_rate.zero.trap: rate 0: poll_interrupt divides by timerRate*2 - firmware crash once a channel is open on that unit (NDevice.cpp:861,867)

net.set_parser.unopened.trap: SET_PARSER with no channel ACKs but binds a parser to a null protocol; the next READ/QUERY/SEEK/TELL crashes the firmware (NDevice.cpp:548-561)

net.query.empty_array.trap: a QUERY whose value is or contains [] dereferences a null child and crashes the firmware (fnjson.cpp:301-307); none of the helper documents has one

net.open.one_field.trap: OPEN with one field (or a single u16) - _params.at(1) throws; fujinet-pc dies, the ESP32 card reboots (FujiBusPacket.h:75-77)

net.open.sd_mode13.trap: SD:// or TNFS:// with aux1 other than 4/6/7/8/9/12 reaches abort() (SD.cpp:56-58)

net.read.header_past_end.trap: a READ in GET_HEADERS mode after the last header indexes past the vector - undefined, may crash (HTTP.cpp:490-495)
